in_class_description_detail: Natural vegetation that covers from 15 to 100% of the ground. It has a lower stratum dominated by natural herbaceous vegetation. It may correspond to what in Uruguay is called “chircal”.

Areas defined by the replacement of the original semi-natural cover or aquatic surface with an artificial cover of impermeable materials characterized by a long lifespan. These are areas constructed or formed by adjacent impermeable structures or connected by streets.
Scattered areas with artificial impermeable cover (15% to 30%), with small crops, forest plantations and natural herbaceous vegetation.
Areas made up of fine to coarse sands and dunes of aeolian origin.

Permanently floodable areas located in zones of little or no slope. A gradient of increasing moisture from the soil to the open water determines a vegetation sequence. When the flooding is temporary, there is a gradual transition to grassland or reedbeds; with permanent flooding, reedbeds or cattail marshes develop. When depth and light permit, submerged or floating aquatic plants become established.

Vegetation dominated by native trees and other plant forms. Includes gallery forest, parkland, mountain forest, and ravine forest. Trees can reach heights of 3 to 8 meters, and ground cover is 65 to 100%. The floristic composition of this ecosystem varies according to the type of forest and environmental conditions.

Vegetation dominated by trees and other native plant forms. Includes gallery forest, parkland, mountain forest, and ravine forest. Trees can reach heights of 3 to 8 meters, and ground cover is 30 to 65%. The floristic composition of this ecosystem varies according to the type of forest and environmental conditions.

in_class_description_detail: Extraction sites where the cover of earth, rock, or aggregate materials is removed by human activity. Sites where mineral extraction and processing activities take place were considered.

This category includes reservoirs/dams (accumulation of water produced by an obstruction in the bed of a river or stream that partially or totally closes its channel) and irrigation canals (constructions that carry water from the collection to the field where it is applied to crops).

This category includes all natural water bodies in the national territory: lakes, lagoons, rivers, streams and areas corresponding to low plains located on the edge of some lagoons and at the mouth of some streams, which remain flooded for several months of the year.

Rice (grass) planting in continuous plots larger than 2 hectares. One crop is grown per year during the summer cycle. Rice cultivation in Uruguay is based on a low-intensity production system, in rotation with pastures and integrated with livestock production (Rice Growers Association).

Large plots (over 2 hectares) with an average farm size of 20 hectares. The entire crop is irrigated using a furrow irrigation system. Surface water resources are used through storage and regulation works or elevated platform pumping systems to ensure water supply.
Herbaceous cultivation of grasses or legumes on large plots larger than 4 to 5 hectares, under rainfed winter conditions. They consist mainly of annual winter cereal or oilseed crops.

in_class_value: Cultivo de invierno y verano (Doble Cultivo)
in_class_description_detail: Herbaceous cultivation of grasses or legumes on large plots, larger than 2 hectares. They consist mainly of annual cereal or oilseed crops, both winter and summer.
Herbaceous cultivation of grasses or legumes on large plots larger than 4 to 5 hectares, under dryland conditions. They consist mainly of annual summer cereal or oilseed crops.

Herbaceous crops on small plots, less than 2 hectares, with irrigation or rainfed farming. This mainly refers to horticultural crops: potatoes, tomatoes, bell peppers, strawberries, eggplant, melons, cucumbers, lettuce, and others.

Plantation of perennial trees or shrubs: citrus, pome and stone fruit trees, vines and olive trees.
plantation on areas less than 5 hectares, generally of various species of Eucalyptus that is used in order to provide shelter and shade to livestock.

Plant ecosystems consisting of a tree layer (palms) and a herbaceous layer. In these ecosystems, the density is between 250 and 500 palms per hectare. There are two large areas in the country where they are concentrated: the “Butiá Palm” (Butiá capitata) groves located in the East (Cerro Largo, Treinta y Tres, Maldonado and Rocha) and the “Yatay Palm” (Butiá yatay) groves located in the Northeast of the country.

Herbaceous vegetation composed mainly of grasses, with the presence of woody plants (less than 15%). The botanical composition, productivity, and seasonality of pastures vary according to soil type and land use.

This category includes areas with herbaceous layers alternating with patches dominated by a relatively continuous rock surface. It is found primarily in transition zones between crystalline rock outcrops and grasslands.

in_class_description_detail: Areas that are temporarily flooded, located in areas with very little or no slope. It is characterized by the absence of waterlogging for most of the year. There is a gradual transition to prairie or grassland.
Herbaceous vegetation composed mainly of grasses in areas of agricultural use that were cultivated in previous years.
Herbaceous vegetation composed mainly of grasses in areas of agricultural use that were cultivated in previous years.

Plant ecosystems consisting mainly of a herbaceous layer with trees (palms) at a density of less than 250 palms per hectare. There are two large areas in the country where they are concentrated: the “Butiá Palm” (Butiá capitata) groves located in the East (Cerro Largo, Treinta y Tres, Maldonado and Rocha) and the “Yatay Palm” (Butiá yatay) groves located in the Northeast of the country.
